control: Identity architecture documented and healthy (cloud-only / hybrid; Entra Connect or Cloud Sync; sync status)
gives: Sync type, last sync time, sync features, sync server name (from Sync_ account / MSOL_ description / ADSync service). ExchangeOnPrem: On-prem federation trust, OAuth auth servers and partner applications - the hybrid plumbing on the Exchange side.
manual: Entra Connect Health (if licensed) for sync errors; record posture in STACK.md.
why: Everything else in identity depends on knowing where the source of truth is and that sync is not silently broken.
target: Documented in STACK.md; sync healthy; owner of the sync server known.

control: MFA enforced for all users via Conditional Access (not legacy per-user MFA); registration coverage
gives: CA policy requiring MFA for all users/apps, Security Defaults state, MFA registration % (members and admins), single-factor interactive sign-ins (P1).
manual: Review the exclusion lists of the MFA policy in the Entra portal.
why: Commodity credential attacks are the #1 initial access path (E8 ML1 MFA).
target: 100% of enabled users registered and enforced through CA; exclusions documented.

control: Strong / phishing-resistant MFA for privileged users; weak methods (SMS/voice) disabled; number matching on
gives: Admin CA policies with authentication strength, SMS/voice method state, number matching, FIDO2/TAP state, admins passwordless-capable.
why: E8 ML2 requires phishing-resistant MFA for privileged access; SMS/voice are trivially phished or SIM-swapped.
target: All admin roles behind phishing-resistant auth strength; SMS/voice off.

control: Legacy authentication blocked (CA block policy; basic auth off in Exchange Online)
gives: CA legacy-auth block policy, Security Defaults, successful legacy sign-ins last 7 days (P1), SMTP AUTH org setting, EXO authentication policies, CAS plan IMAP/POP defaults. ExchangeOnPrem: Basic authentication on Exchange virtual directories and Outlook Anywhere, plus POP/IMAP login types. On-prem Exchange has no Conditional Access, so these are not covered by the Entra legacy-auth block.
manual: Without P1: Entra portal > Sign-in logs filtered by legacy client apps.
why: Legacy protocols bypass MFA entirely.
target: Blocked; zero legacy successes in 30 days.

control: Privileged role hygiene: Global Admin count 2-4, dedicated cloud-only admin accounts, least-privilege roles, PIM/JIT where licensed
gives: Global Admin count and names, privileged users with licence/mailbox, synced admins, guest admins, service principals in roles, PIM eligible count (P2); on-prem Domain Admins for cross-check.
why: Standing global admin on daily-driver accounts is the most common tenant-loss pattern (E8 RAP).
target: 2-4 GAs; all admins dedicated accounts; least privilege roles; PIM if licensed.

control: Break-glass accounts: two exist, cloud-only, excluded from CA, credentials vaulted, sign-in alert configured
gives: Accounts excluded from every all-user CA policy (break-glass candidates).
manual: Vault entry (client vault / CyberArk), sign-in alert rule (Sentinel/Log Analytics/Huntress), last test date (LOG.md).
why: Lock-out from a CA or MFA outage becomes a P1 without them; unmonitored ones are a backdoor.
target: Two accounts, vaulted, alerting, tested.

control: Partner access is GDAP (not DAP) with least-privilege roles; bA access via Lighthouse named admin accounts; no shared customer admin accounts in CyberArk
gives: Partner-style principals (Partner Tier2 Support, Directory Synchronization Accounts) in customer roles.
manual: M365 Lighthouse > Tenants > GDAP relationship, roles and expiry; Partner Center for residual DAP; CyberArk safe review for shared customer admin accounts.
why: bA policy (KB0012228/KB0012557): named-account audit trail; shared accounts are an audit and insurance finding.
target: GDAP least privilege; no DAP; no shared standing admin accounts.

control: Guest and external identity governance: stale guests removed, collaboration settings restricted, access reviews where licensed
gives: Guest count, inactive guests, who can invite, guest role, cross-tenant default inbound setting.
manual: Access review configuration (Entra > Identity Governance) if P2.
why: Guests accumulate silently and retain access to Teams/SharePoint data indefinitely.
target: No guest inactive > 90 days; invite restricted; review cadence exists.

control: Account lifecycle: stale users/computers disabled, JML (joiner-mover-leaver) process defined, service accounts inventoried with owners
gives: Stale enabled users (cloud and AD), stale computers, password-never-expires, password-not-required, service-account-like accounts, gMSA count.
manual: JML process document (SNOW KB) and owner list for service accounts.
why: Leavers with live accounts and orphaned service accounts are the quiet way in.
target: Stale objects < 2%; JML documented; service account register current.

control: On-prem AD DS health (if hybrid): supported DC OS, replication clean, FSMO/DNS sane, KRBTGT rotated, recycle bin on, legacy protocols disabled
gives: DC OS support, replication health, FSMO, recycle bin, KRBTGT age, SYSVOL type, kerberoastable/AS-REP/DES/SIDHistory/unconstrained delegation, DC SMBv1/LDAP signing/channel binding/NTLM level.
why: An unhealthy or unhardened AD undermines every cloud control and is the ransomware pivot point.
target: Healthy replication, supported DCs, KRBTGT < 180 d, legacy protocols off.

control: Credential policy: Entra Password Protection (incl. on-prem agent), sensible expiry policy, Windows LAPS for local admin passwords
gives: Entra Password Protection settings, default and fine-grained AD password policies, LAPS coverage (Entra-backed and AD-backed), LAPS policy on hosts.
why: Reused/guessable passwords and shared local admin passwords enable lateral movement (E8 ML2: local admin creds unique and managed).
target: Password Protection on; LAPS on all Windows endpoints and member servers.

control: Conditional Access baseline: compliant/hybrid-joined device for corporate apps, unsupported platforms blocked, session controls for unmanaged devices, named locations
gives: CA baseline: compliant/hybrid device, platform block, session controls, location blocks, named locations.
why: MFA alone does not stop token theft or access from unmanaged devices.
target: Documented CA baseline with the four core policies enabled.

control: Identity Protection / risky sign-in handling (P2): risk policies enabled, risky users remediated, alerts routed to MDR/SOC
gives: Risk-based CA policies, risky users and 30-day detections (P2). Reports 'not licensed' when P2 is absent.
why: Licensed detection that nobody watches is a paid-for gap.
target: Policies on; no unremediated risky users > 7 days; alerts monitored.

control: SaaS SSO coverage and app consent governance: key apps behind Entra SSO; user consent to unverified apps blocked; admin consent workflow
gives: User consent setting, admin consent workflow, user-consented OAuth grants, app registration rights.
manual: SSO coverage of the client's key SaaS: compare Enterprise applications list with the client's SaaS register (AZ-08).
why: OAuth consent phishing and orphaned SaaS logins bypass every device and MFA control.
target: Consent restricted; workflow on; critical SaaS on SSO.

control: Tenant baseline: Microsoft Secure Score tracked, top actions actioned or formally risk-accepted, quarterly M365 Health Report top-3 closed
gives: Secure Score %, 90-day trend, largest improvement actions and category gaps.
manual: Status of last quarter's top-3 (LOG.md / last quarterly report).
why: Handbook expects top-3 priorities per customer per quarter; Secure Score is the shared yardstick with the client.
target: Score trending up; last quarter's top-3 closed or re-planned with dates.

control: Email authentication: SPF (single record, < 10 lookups, -all), DKIM on all sending domains and third-party senders, DMARC at quarantine/reject with reporting
gives: Per domain: MX/gateway, SPF (records, all-mechanism, lookup count), DKIM selectors live, DMARC policy/pct/rua, MTA-STS/TLS-RPT; EXO DKIM enabled per domain; parked-domain check. ExchangeOnPrem: On-prem accepted domains and email address policies (what this server is authoritative for, and therefore what SPF must cover).
manual: DMARC aggregate report review (dmarcian/Mimecast); Mimecast DKIM selectors if not in the default selector list.
why: Spoofing of the client's own domain drives BEC losses; DMARC p=none is not protection.
target: All domains SPF -all, DKIM aligned, DMARC p=quarantine or reject with reports reviewed.

control: Inbound mail protection: Mimecast or Defender for Office 365 with impersonation/anti-phish, Safe Links/Attachments (or URL Protect/Attachment Protect), connectors locked to the gateway
gives: Preset security policies, anti-phish impersonation/mailbox intelligence, Safe Links/Attachments, malware/spam policies, inbound partner connector lock-down, gateway detection from MX/connectors. ExchangeOnPrem: On-prem send/receive connectors, smart hosts, TLS requirements, and receive connectors permitting anonymous relay (including unrestricted 0.0.0.0-255.255.255.255 open relays).
manual: Mimecast policy configuration (Mimecast console).
why: Email remains the top delivery channel; an open EXO connector lets attackers bypass the gateway.
target: Gateway policies on for all users; MX bypass closed.

control: Mailbox hygiene: external auto-forwarding blocked, forwarding report clean, mailbox auditing on, shared mailboxes sign-in blocked, inactive licensed mailboxes reviewed
gives: Auto-forward settings (policy, remote domains, transport rules), mailbox forwarding to external domains, shared mailboxes with sign-in enabled, inactive mailboxes, audit state, SCL-bypass rules. ExchangeOnPrem: On-prem transport rules that redirect/BCC/copy, remote domains allowing auto-forward, and mailbox-level forwarding on remaining on-prem mailboxes.
manual: Inbox rules per mailbox unless run with -CheckInboxRules.
why: Auto-forward rules are the classic post-compromise persistence; inactive licensed mailboxes are pure waste.
target: Forwarding blocked; no unexplained external forwards; shared mailbox sign-in blocked.

control: Exchange on-prem residual: no Exchange 2016/2019 (EoS 14 Oct 2025) - migrated to Exchange SE or removed; last-Exchange-server for recipient management handled
gives: Exchange server objects and versions in AD, hybrid objects in EXO, autodiscover/MX pointing on-prem, Exchange binaries on hosts. ExchangeOnPrem: On-prem Exchange servers with true build from ExSetup (security-update level, not just the CU), support status, hybrid configuration and HCW features, org relationships and intra-org connectors, mailboxes still hosted on-prem vs RemoteMailbox, public folders, and whether the server is management-only.
manual: - Hybrid Agent (modern hybrid) publishing is not visible from Exchange - confirm in the M365 admin centre / on the agent host. Decommission decisions and Exchange SE licensing sit with the client.
why: Unsupported Exchange is internet-facing, unpatched and directly exploitable.
target: No unsupported Exchange; hybrid management path documented.

control: SharePoint/OneDrive sharing: external sharing scoped, Anyone links off or expiring, default link type internal, unmanaged-device session controls, guest expiry
gives: Tenant sharing capability, external resharing, domain restriction, legacy auth protocols, idle session sign-out, unmanaged sync restriction; OWA third-party storage.
manual: SPO shell (Get-SPOTenant): RequireAnonymousLinksExpireInDays, DefaultSharingLinkType, ConditionalAccessPolicy; guest expiry; sensitivity labels on sites.
why: Over-permissive links are the most common M365 data leakage path and an easy insurer/auditor finding.
target: Sharing restricted per policy; Anyone links off/expiring; defaults internal.

control: Teams governance: external access/federation and guest access deliberate, meeting policies (anonymous join, lobby), third-party app policies, team sprawl managed
gives: Federation/allowed domains, consumer access, guest access, meeting anonymous join/lobby, app permission policy, third-party storage in Teams.
manual: Teams admin centre if the MicrosoftTeams module is not installed; team creation governance.
why: Open federation enables Teams-based phishing; uncontrolled apps and guests expand the attack surface.
target: Deliberate, documented settings; no 'allow all' defaults left unreviewed.

control: Data protection: retention policies for Exchange/SharePoint/Teams, DLP baseline (AU PII/TFN/credit card), sensitivity labels where licensed, audit log retention
gives: Retention policies and scope, DLP policies and mode, sensitivity/retention labels and policies, litigation holds, archives.
manual: Audit log retention policies (E5), mapping to the client's legal obligations.
why: Retention is not backup, but its absence is a legal/regulatory exposure; DLP catches the accidental send.
target: Retention + baseline DLP in place and documented.

control: Microsoft 365 backup (third-party) covering Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams; coverage %, last job success, restore tested
manual: M365 backup console (Veeam for M365 / Datto SaaS / AvePoint): coverage, last job, retention, restore test; BAMS backup line items in eFO.
why: Microsoft's shared-responsibility model leaves data recovery to the customer (E8 RB).
target: 100% coverage, jobs green, restore tested.

control: Licensing fit: SKU inventory vs assigned vs active; unused licences; security features licensed but not deployed (P1/P2, Defender for Endpoint, Intune, Purview)
gives: SKU purchased vs assigned, unassigned paid seats, entitlement detection (P1/P2/Intune/Defender/Purview), licensed accounts with no sign-in, licensed shared mailboxes, inactive mailboxes.
manual: Active-usage reports (M365 admin centre > Usage); NCE renewal dates (eFO).
why: Clients pay for controls they do not use, or run controls they are not licensed for.
target: < 5% unassigned; licensed security features deployed or consciously deferred.

control: Service health and Message Centre monitored; upcoming retirements/breaking changes tracked in LOG.md
gives: Message centre 'Plan for change' items last 90 days, major changes, action-required dates.
manual: Named owner; track relevant items in LOG.md.
why: Microsoft retires features on a schedule; surprises become incidents.
target: Named owner; changes tracked.

control: Alert routing: security/compliance alerts and tenant notifications go to a monitored mailbox or MDR (Huntress ITDR / Rapid7), technical contact current
gives: Tenant technical/security notification addresses; count of untriaged Defender alerts.
manual: Defender portal > Settings > Email notifications recipients; Huntress/Rapid7 M365 connector health.
why: Alerts sent to a departed admin's mailbox are alerts nobody sees.
target: All alerts reach a monitored destination.

control: Device inventory and management coverage: every workstation/laptop/mobile enrolled in Intune (or GPO/ConfigMgr) and in RMM; unmanaged device count
gives: Intune device count/OS/stale/personal, Entra device count/trust/managed/compliant, host-check counts, AD computer objects.
manual: EDR console device count; HR headcount (PROFILE) for the reconciliation.
why: You cannot patch, protect or wipe what you do not manage; coverage gaps are also BAMS billing gaps.
target: Counts reconcile within 2%; every corporate device in MDM + RMM + EDR.

control: OS currency: Windows 11 only (Windows 10 EoS 14 Oct 2025; ESU only as documented exception), macOS n/n-1, feature update rings defined
gives: Windows 10 vs 11 counts from every source, build distribution, feature-update policies.
why: Unsupported OS = no security updates (E8 PO ML1: unsupported OS replaced).
target: Zero unsupported OS without documented ESU/exception; rings defined.

control: OS patch compliance: workstations patched within 1 month (E8 ML1), critical/exploited within 48 h where internet-facing; reboot compliance; reporting
gives: Update rings and deferrals, host last-patch age distribution, pending reboots, live WU scan (optional).
manual: Exact compliance % vs SLA: Intune update reports / N-Central patch report.
why: Patch latency is the single largest measurable exposure.
target: >= 95% within 30 days; < 5% stale; process documented.

control: Third-party application patching: browsers, Office/M365 Apps, PDF, Java, collaboration clients patched within 2 weeks (E8 PA ML1); unsupported apps removed
gives: Known-vulnerable/EoL versions on hosts (7-Zip, WinRAR, PuTTY, Flash, Java, Office perpetual), browser versions, Intune detected apps watchlist.
manual: N-Central / NinjaOne third-party patch compliance report; Intune Enterprise App Management coverage.
why: Browsers and PDF readers are the applications actually exploited on endpoints.
target: Automated 3rd-party patching, >= 90% within 14 days, EoL apps removed.

control: Endpoint vulnerability scanning: Defender Vulnerability Management or Rapid7 IVM agent on all devices; cadence per E8 ML1; critical findings aged < 30 days
manual: Defender Vulnerability Management dashboard (security.microsoft.com) or Rapid7 InsightVM: agent coverage, scan cadence, exploited criticals > 30 days.
why: E8 ML1 requires scanning (weekly apps, fortnightly OS) - patching without scanning is unverified.
target: >= 98% coverage; no exploited criticals > 30 days.

control: EDR/AV coverage and health: Trend / CrowdStrike / Defender for Endpoint on 100% of devices, sensors healthy (reported <= 7 days), tamper protection on, Huntress agent alongside
gives: EDR/AV product per host, hosts with none, Defender mode/tamper protection/signature age.
manual: EDR console inactive sensors; Huntress portal agent list; alert routing confirmation.
why: EDR is the control that turns a breach into an alert; unhealthy sensors are invisible gaps. CrowdStrike removal needs a customer-generated key - know the process before a P1.
target: 100% coverage, < 2% inactive, tamper protection on.

control: Disk encryption: BitLocker enforced with recovery keys escrowed to Entra/Intune (or AD); FileVault on macOS; compliance report
gives: Intune isEncrypted %, BitLocker recovery keys escrowed to Entra, OS-volume protection and recovery protector on hosts, encryption policies.
why: Lost laptops become notifiable data breaches without encryption evidence.
target: >= 98% encrypted with escrowed keys.

control: Local administrator restriction: users are not local admins; Windows LAPS on every device; documented elevation path (EPM / RMM / temporary)
gives: Entra LAPS coverage, Intune LAPS policy, AD LAPS attributes, non-standard local admins per host, built-in admin state/password age.
manual: Elevation request process (EPM/RMM) documentation.
why: Local admin defeats application control, EDR tamper protection and macro settings (E8 RAP).
target: No standard users as local admin; LAPS 100%.

control: Application control on workstations (Airlock / WDAC / AppLocker): executables, scripts, installers, DLLs, HTA/CHM/CPL restricted; user profile and temp paths covered (E8 AC ML1)
gives: AppLocker enforcement per collection, WDAC enforcement status and active policies, Airlock/ThreatLocker agent presence, Intune app-control policies.
manual: Airlock portal: enforcement mode per group, blocked-event review, exception process.
why: Application control is the E8 control with the highest ransomware-prevention value and the one most often missing.
target: Enforced on all workstations for the E8 file types; audit-mode only as a time-boxed step.

control: Microsoft Office macros: blocked from the internet, disabled for users without business need, AV scanning on, settings locked (E8 MAC ML1); Win32 API calls blocked (ML2)
gives: Per-host macro policy (VBAWarnings, block-from-internet, AMSI scope), ASR Win32 macro rule, Intune settings-catalog/ADMX macro settings.
why: Macro-borne malware is still a leading delivery mechanism; user-changeable settings make the control cosmetic.
target: All four ML1 requirements enforced; ML2 Win32 block on.

control: User application hardening: browser hardening (no Java/ads from internet, settings locked), IE11 removed, ASR rules for Office/PDF child processes and injection, PowerShell v2 removed, script block/command-line logging (E8 UAH ML1/ML2)
gives: ASR rule states (host and policy), IE11 feature, PowerShell v2, script-block/command-line logging, LLMNR, Java, browser policies and force-installed extensions, Edge/Chrome versions.
manual: OLE package activation and PDF hardening specifics (E8 ML2) if not visible in policy names.
why: Closes the paths exploits and macros use to get from a document to a shell.
target: ML1 browser controls + core ASR rules in block mode; logging on.

control: Compliance policies integrated with Conditional Access: encryption, AV, firewall, OS minimum, Defender risk score; non-compliant device count and grace periods
gives: Compliance policies and settings, non-compliant device %, CA policies requiring compliance.
why: Compliance policies make device state enforceable through CA rather than advisory.
target: < 5% non-compliant; CA-enforced.

control: Provisioning and SOE: Autopilot registration for new devices, baseline profile documented, naming standard, Autopilot & Intune best-practice checklist applied
gives: Autopilot profiles/assignments, registered devices, ESP, ADMX profile count, autopilot-enrolled %.
manual: SOE document currency (SNOW KB / SharePoint); bA Autopilot & Intune checklist deviations.
why: Consistent builds are the foundation for every other endpoint control and cut ticket volume.
target: Autopilot in use; SOE documented < 12 months old.

control: Mobile devices: iOS/Android access controlled by MAM/app protection (or MDM), PIN/biometric, selective wipe tested, BYOD stance documented
gives: App protection policies (iOS/Android/Windows, PIN, save-as), mobile devices under MDM, enrolment restrictions, CA app-protection policy, Exchange mobile policy.
manual: BYOD stance document.
why: Corporate mail on unmanaged phones is the most common uncontrolled data copy.
target: App protection enforced via CA for all mobile access.

control: Peripheral and host controls: USB removable storage policy, Windows Firewall enforced on all profiles, screen lock <= 15 min, printer driver policy (Point and Print restrictions)
gives: Firewall profiles, screen lock, removable storage, Point and Print, AutoLogon on hosts; Intune restriction/settings-catalog equivalents.
why: Cheap controls that close common audit findings and lateral-movement paths.
target: Policies deployed to all devices.

control: Endpoint lifecycle: device age, warranty status, Windows 11 ineligible units, refresh plan and budget signalled to SDM/CAM
gives: Manufacturer/model/serial per host (hosts.csv), Intune models.
manual: Warranty lookups by serial (Dell/HP), purchase dates, refresh plan (LIC-01 register).
why: Ageing fleets generate tickets and block OS currency; refresh is billable project work.
target: Register exists; refresh plan agreed; no device > 6 years in production.

control: Server inventory accurate across SNOW CIs, eFO, Orion and vCenter/emPOWER: counts match, IP/NAT IP present, role and owner documented
gives: Server lists from AD (active 60 days), reachable hosts, Azure VMs, vCenter VMs, Veeam inventory - one side of the reconciliation.
manual: SNOW CI export, eFO Cloud Services, Orion node list to diff against; raise CI corrections.
why: CI gaps break monitoring, billing and P1 response (handbook: CI discrepancies form).
target: Zero unexplained differences; all CIs complete.

control: Server OS support status: no Windows Server 2012/2012 R2 (ESU ends Oct 2026), Server 2016 plan (EoS 12 Jan 2027), Server 2022 mainstream ends 13 Oct 2026; Linux distros in support
gives: OS families with support status and EoS dates from every source; legacy guests in vSphere. ExchangeOnPrem: Exchange server roles, editions and sites (Windows OS support for the same hosts comes from the Servers collector). Citrix and ParallelsRas: the session-host and VDA hostnames to reconcile against the Servers collector - these carry every user session, so an out-of-support build here has the widest blast radius in the estate.
why: Unsupported OS breaches E8 PO ML1 and cyber-insurance conditions; 2016 is the next cliff for most clients.
target: No EoS OS; migration plan with dates for anything within 12 months.

control: Server patch compliance: monthly cadence within 1 month (E8 ML1), internet-facing within 48 h for critical/exploited; maintenance windows agreed; failed/pending reboots
gives: Last-patch age, pending reboots, uptime, update source per server; Azure Update Manager assessment. ExchangeOnPrem: Exchange security-update currency per server against the published build table - the CU-only version hides missing SUs.
manual: N-Central patch status per server; maintenance windows (STACK.md). Confirm the current build table at aka.ms/exchangebuildnumbers; the collector's table is a point-in-time copy.
why: Servers are patched less consistently than endpoints and are the higher-value target.
target: >= 95% within 30 days; windows documented; exceptions listed.

control: Server hardening baseline: CIS/Microsoft baseline, SMBv1 off, TLS 1.0/1.1 off, RDP not internet-exposed + NLA, EDR on servers, unnecessary roles removed, application control on internet-facing servers (E8 ML2)
gives: SMBv1, TLS 1.0/1.1, RDP NLA, firewall profiles, WDigest, NTLM level, UAC, spooler, EDR on servers, application control on servers, listeners. ExchangeOnPrem: Windows Extended Protection per virtual directory vs the Microsoft-recommended values, SSL offloading on Outlook Anywhere, TLS 1.0/1.1/1.2 and LmCompatibilityLevel per Exchange server (and whether TLS is consistent across them), external URLs published on each virtual directory, and any Exchange setting overrides.
manual: Internet exposure of RDP (firewall NAT - see FortiGate NET-04); CIS baseline evidence. Extended Protection and TLS are read over WinRM; where a server is unreachable, run the Exchange Health Checker (aka.ms/ExchangeHealthChecker) on it.
why: Default builds carry known-weak protocols; internet-facing servers are the E8 ML2 application-control scope.
target: Baseline applied and evidenced; no exposed RDP; EDR 100% on servers.

control: Privileged access to servers: admin via jump host/RDM with CyberArk-sourced credentials, no direct RDP from user VLAN, tiered admin accounts, gMSA/managed service accounts
gives: Domain/Enterprise/Schema Admins and operator groups, Protected Users, non-standard local admins on servers.
manual: Jump-host enforcement (firewall rule user VLAN -> RDP), CyberArk/RDM usage.
why: E8 ML2 requires jump servers and separate privileged environments; flat admin access is how ransomware spreads.
target: Jump-host-only admin, dedicated tiered accounts, DA <= 5.

control: Hypervisor platform health: vSphere/Hyper-V version in support (vSphere 7 end of general support was 2 Oct 2025), host firmware currency, HA/DRS configured, N+1 capacity, datastore free >= 20%, stale snapshots, VMware licensing status post-Broadcom
gives: vCenter/host versions, HA/DRS, datastore free %, stale snapshots, tools status, licences; virtual %/tools via host check when PowerCLI absent.
manual: emPOWER VCD/vCenter for hosted platforms; Hyper-V manually; VMware subscription status (Broadcom portal).
why: The hypervisor is a single point of failure for the whole estate and a licensing cost risk.
target: Supported version, N+1, no stale snapshots, licensing current.

control: Capacity and performance: CPU/RAM/storage headroom and 12-month growth trend; over/under-provisioned VMs; storage latency alerts
gives: Current cluster CPU/memory utilisation, >= 8 vCPU VMs, low-space volumes, Advisor right-sizing.
manual: 90-day trends and forecast: Orion capacity reports / vCenter performance charts.
why: Capacity surprises become emergency purchases; right-sizing is a visible value-add (and billable in emPOWER terms).
target: >= 6 months headroom; right-sizing recommendations issued.

control: File services: share permissions (no Everyone/Authenticated Users modify), DFS-N/DFS-R health, quotas/FSRM, migration candidates to SharePoint/Azure Files
gives: Non-admin shares per server and share-level ACLs granting Change/Full to Everyone/Authenticated Users/Domain Users.
manual: NTFS ACL audit of top-level folders; DFS-R health (dfsrdiag / Get-DfsrState); SharePoint Migration Assessment.
why: Open shares are the ransomware blast radius and the data-governance blind spot.
target: No broad-write shares; DFS healthy; migration position documented.

control: Database and application servers: SQL versions in support (SQL 2014 and 2016 are out of support - 9 Jul 2024 and 14 Jul 2026; ESU only), backups (full + log) and recovery model, application owners and vendor support contracts documented
gives: SQL instances/versions/editions with support status, hosts advertising SQL SPNs, Veeam application-aware processing. ExchangeOnPrem: Exchange mailbox databases, mount state, DAG membership and copy/content-index health.
manual: Recovery model vs backup type (SQL query); LoB vendor support contracts.
why: Line-of-business apps are why the client exists; SQL EoS and untested backups are the risk.
target: Supported SQL; backups match recovery model; app owners known.

control: Certificates and PKI: internal CA health (CRL/AIA publishing, CA OS support), certificate expiry inventory, public cert automation plan (public TLS max lifetime 200 days since 15 Mar 2026, 100 days from Mar 2027, 47 days from Mar 2029 - CA/B Forum SC-081)
gives: Expiring/expired certificates with private keys on servers, enterprise CAs and hosts, CAA records. ExchangeOnPrem: Exchange certificates with expiry and self-signed-bound-to-IIS detection, plus the OAuth (Auth) certificate expiry - the one that silently breaks hybrid free/busy and OWA/ECP sign-in. NetScaler: appliance certificates with days to expiry and SHA-1 signatures. ParallelsRas: RAS gateway certificates with expiry.
manual: pkiview.msc / certutil -URL for CRL/AIA health; GeoCerts inventory; ACME automation plan.
why: Expired certificates cause outages; manual renewal will not scale as lifetimes shrink.
target: Inventory current; nothing expiring < 30 days unowned; automation plan for public certs.

control: Core services: NTP hierarchy, DNS (scavenging, forwarders not ISP, split-brain documented), DHCP failover and scope utilisation
gives: DNS scavenging/aging/forwarders and PDC/member-server time sources (AD, Servers). Dhcp: authorised servers and reachability, scope utilisation and failover relationships, lease durations, option hygiene (DNS/router/domain/NTP incl. public resolvers handed to clients), dynamic DNS registration credential and name protection, audit logging, database backup path and interval, conflict detection. Nps: RADIUS service presence, state and whether there is a second one.
manual: DHCP served by a firewall or appliance rather than Windows is not covered - read it from that device.
why: Quiet services that cause loud outages (Kerberos time skew, scope exhaustion).
target: All three healthy and documented.

control: Print, RDS and legacy services: print server hardening (Point and Print), RDS host and CAL licensing, legacy runtimes (.NET, Java) on supported versions
gives: Print servers and Point-and-Print restriction, spooler on non-print servers, RDS hosts, IIS, .NET below 4.8.
manual: RDS CAL counts and licensing mode (RD Licensing Manager). Citrix, Parallels RAS and the published-application platform as a whole are covered by SRV-14.
why: Print spooler and remote-desktop hosts are recurring CVE targets and licence-compliance traps.
target: Hardened, licensed, supported.

control: Linux estate: distro support status, automated patching (unattended-upgrades/dnf-automatic/Ansible), SSH hardening (key-only, no root), monitoring and backup agents, domain integration (SSSD) if applicable
manual: Linux hosts are not covered by the Windows host check: over SSH check /etc/os-release, unattended-upgrades/dnf-automatic, sshd_config (PermitRootLogin, PasswordAuthentication), monitoring/backup agents.
why: Linux boxes are often 'someone else's' and fall outside the Windows-centric patch and monitoring loops.
target: All Linux hosts supported, patched, monitored, backed up.

control: Published application and VDI platform (Citrix CVAD / Parallels RAS / RDS): farm version in support, broker and gateway redundancy, session host and VDA health, licensing model and entitlement headroom, gateway exposure and MFA
gives: Citrix: site name and controller version placed on the LTSR/CR lifecycle table, Local Host Cache, machine catalogs and delivery groups (maintenance mode, unregistered machines), VDA registration state and version spread with last-deregistration reasons, licence server, edition, model and concurrent usage, session and Workspace-app version mix, site database connection. ParallelsRas: farm and site layout, RAS version against the Parallels lifecycle table, publishing agent and secure gateway counts and health, HALB, RD session host agent state and NeedsUpdate, MFA providers and SAML identity providers, licence type and concurrent-user headroom, published items and full desktops. NetScaler: the Citrix Gateway vServers fronting the farm, what authentication is bound to each, and ICA-only mode.
manual: RDS CAL counts and licensing mode (RD Licensing Manager); StoreFront configuration and beacon setup; Citrix DaaS (Citrix Cloud) tenants, which need a Citrix Cloud API client and are not covered by this toolkit; profile management (FSLogix / Citrix UPM) health and container sizing; the session-host image build and update process; STA server list on the gateway.
why: The entire user population reaches its applications through this platform, so a single broker, an expired gateway certificate or an out-of-support farm version is a total outage rather than a degraded service - and the session hosts are usually excluded from endpoint tooling because they are filed as servers.
target: Farm version in support; publishing agent/controller and gateway both redundant; MFA on every published gateway; session hosts inside the patching, EDR and application-control coverage counts; licence entitlement, headroom and renewal date known.

control: Network documentation current: L3 diagram (< 12 months), VLAN/IP schema in Netbox, WAN/ISP circuits and carrier contacts recorded
gives: AD sites and subnet count for comparison with the diagram. Dhcp: every DHCP-served subnet with its range, name and reservation count - the closest thing to evidence of the live IP schema, and usually more current than the diagram.
manual: SharePoint diagram revision date; Netbox prefixes vs live config; circuit register.
why: Handbook: network changes require diagram updates; incidents without a diagram take twice as long.
target: Diagram < 12 months and accurate; IPAM current; circuits documented.

control: Firewall platform: model in support, FortiOS on a recommended mature branch (per PSIRT), HA pair, config backed up in FortiManager, management not internet-exposed, individual admin accounts, MFA
gives: Model/serial/firmware, newer patches in branch, HA mode/peers, admin trusted hosts and 2FA, management on WAN, admin port/timeout, FortiAnalyzer/syslog, licences. NetScaler: firmware branch against the 7-year release cycle with end-of-maintenance and end-of-life dates, HA node state and sync, management IPs with GUI/SSH/Telnet exposed and unrestricted, local system users and nsroot presence, NTP and syslog targets.
manual: PSIRT comparison for the running build; FortiManager config backup status; model end-of-support (Fortinet product life cycle). NetScaler: Citrix security bulletins for the running build.
why: Fortinet edge devices are actively exploited within days of PSIRT advisories; unmanaged firmware is the top network risk.
target: Supported model, current recommended firmware, HA (or documented risk), management locked down.

control: Firewall policy hygiene: no any/any, unused rules (zero hits > 90 days) removed, logging on all policies, security profiles (IPS/AV/web filter/app control/DNS filter) on internet-bound policies, geo-blocking
gives: Policy table: any/any, logging disabled, internet-bound policies without UTM profiles, zero-hit policies, geo usage.
manual: SSL inspection posture; FortiAnalyzer 90-day hit history if live counters were reset.
why: Policy sprawl hides risky rules; unlogged rules blind the SIEM.
target: Clean policy set with profiles and logging on every internet-bound rule.

control: Internet-facing exposure: external scan of all public IPs; every open port justified; no RDP/SMB/database exposed; SSL-VPN tunnel mode (removed in FortiOS 7.6.3) migrated to IPsec (TCP/443 option) or ZTNA
gives: WAN-sourced accept policies and risky published services, Azure NSG exposure and public IPs, internal listeners. NetScaler: TLS protocol versions still enabled per SSL vServer (SSLv2/v3, TLS 1.0/1.1), HSTS, and load-balanced vServers that are administratively up but effectively down.
manual: External scan of all public IPs (Rapid7 InsightVM external / LionGard / Shodan).
why: Exposed services and legacy VPN portals are the initial access of choice for ransomware crews.
target: Only justified services exposed, behind IPS; VPN modern and MFA-protected.

control: Remote access: VPN/ZTNA requires MFA (SAML/Entra), device posture checks, split-tunnel policy documented, contractor access segregated and time-bound
gives: SSL-VPN state/port, IPsec dial-up and site-to-site, SAML/LDAP/RADIUS sources, local users and FortiToken 2FA. Nps: VPN-shaped network policies and whether the Entra MFA NPS extension is installed on every NPS server rather than just one. NetScaler: Citrix Gateway vServers and the authentication bound to each - SAML, RADIUS or LDAP-only. ParallelsRas: RAS MFA providers, criteria and SAML identity providers.
manual: Entra enterprise app claims for VPN SAML; contractor group membership/expiry.
why: VPN without MFA is the cheapest credential-stuffing target on the internet (E8 MFA).
target: MFA on all remote access; no standing local VPN accounts.

control: Segmentation: user/server/guest/IoT-OT/voice/management VLANs separated by policy; guest wireless isolated; printers, cameras, BMS not on user VLAN
gives: Interfaces referenced by policies and count of inter-VLAN accept policies.
manual: Switch VLAN configuration; diagram; guest/IoT isolation test.
why: Flat networks turn one infected laptop into a whole-of-business outage.
target: Segmented with default-deny between zones; guest/IoT isolated.

control: Switching and wireless: firmware currency, loop protection, uplink redundancy, PoE budget, WPA2/3-Enterprise with 802.1X (no corporate PSK), controller/cloud licence expiry
gives: Nps: wireless (IEEE 802.11) network policies on NPS, which evidence 802.1X for corporate Wi-Fi rather than a shared PSK.
manual: Meraki dashboard / Aruba Central / FortiSwitch: firmware vs recommended, licence expiry, the SSID-to-policy binding and any parallel PSK SSID, STP/loop protection.
why: Access-layer neglect causes the intermittent faults that consume service-desk time.
target: Supported firmware; 802.1X for corporate Wi-Fi; licences > 90 days.

control: Network monitoring coverage: every firewall/switch/AP/UPS in Orion (or LogicMonitor/Meraki) with SNMPv3, utilisation alerts, config backup (NCM/FortiManager), syslog to FortiAnalyzer/Rapid7
gives: FortiAnalyzer/syslog shipping and NTP on the firewall.
manual: Orion node list vs device inventory (SNMPv3); NCM/FortiManager config backups; Rapid7 log sources.
why: Unmonitored network devices are diagnosed by user complaints.
target: 100% of network devices monitored, backed up and logging.

control: WAN and internet resilience: dual ISP or SD-WAN with tested failover, 4G/5G backup where appropriate, single points of failure listed, carrier SLA known
gives: Site-to-site tunnel list.
manual: SD-WAN/dual-WAN configuration, failover test records, carrier SLAs (PROFILE sites).
why: Cloud-first clients lose everything when the single link drops.
target: Critical sites have tested failover; SPOFs accepted in writing or planned.

control: DNS and domain hygiene: registrar (TPP) and DNS (EasyDNS) access controlled, registrar lock, expiry > 6 months, CAA record, stale/dangling records removed (subdomain takeover)
gives: NS provider, CAA, DNSSEC, MTA-STS/TLS-RPT per domain.
manual: TPP Wholesale: expiry, registrar lock, contacts; EasyDNS zone export for dangling records.
why: Domain loss or hijack is total business outage; dangling CNAMEs are free phishing infrastructure.
target: Locked, current, clean zone, CAA set.

control: Network access control: 802.1X/MAB or port security on wired, rogue device detection, DHCP snooping/dynamic ARP inspection where supported
gives: Nps: RADIUS clients with their addresses and whether Message-Authenticator is required, shared-secret length (never the value), wired/Ethernet network policies, the authentication methods the policy set allows (EAP-TLS / PEAP / MS-CHAPv2 / PAP), and enabled policies with no group condition.
manual: Switch configs (which ports actually enforce 802.1X/MAB, port security, unused ports disabled); NAC console (FortiNAC/Meraki/ClearPass); client-side certificate validation for PEAP, which the server cannot prove.
why: Anyone who can plug in should not get the server VLAN.
target: Port-level control on user-accessible ports.

control: Voice/UC and special networks: Teams Phone/SBC or PBX support status, QoS, emergency-call location, BMS/CCTV/OT firmware and isolation
manual: Teams admin centre (Teams Phone/SBC), PBX console support status, OT/CCTV/BMS inventory and vendor remote access.
why: Legacy PBX and OT devices are unpatched Linux boxes with vendor remote access.
target: Supported, isolated, vendor access controlled.

control: Backup coverage: every production server/VM, database and SaaS workload is in a backup job; unprotected list is empty
gives: Powered-on VMs without a restore point in 7 days, Azure VMs without a backup item.
manual: vminfo.empowercloud (emPOWER last backup) for hosted workloads; BAMS backup line items (eFO); physical/agent-protected servers.
why: The item nobody added to the job is the one that gets encrypted (E8 RB).
target: 100% of production protected; contract matches reality.

control: Backup success and monitoring: 30-day success >= 98%, failures actioned within 24 h, job alerts to bA Backup team/NOC, warnings not chronically ignored
gives: 30-day session results, success rate, jobs with repeated failures/warnings, disabled schedules, copy jobs.
manual: Orion backup monitors; SNOW incidents for backup failures (actioned within 24 h?).
why: A green dashboard with 40 days of warnings is a failed backup in waiting.
target: >= 98% success; no failure unactioned > 24 h.

control: Retention, RPO and RTO documented per system tier and agreed with the business; regulatory retention (e.g. 7 years financial records) reflected; matches contract
gives: Configured retention per job.
manual: Agreed RPO/RTO/retention table (SoW/BAMS scope, PROFILE.md, DR plan).
why: Without agreed targets, every restore conversation becomes a dispute.
target: Documented, agreed, and matching configuration.

control: 3-2-1 and immutability: second copy offsite (emPOWER cross-DC / Azure / object storage), immutable or air-gapped copy, repository not domain-joined, separate credentials, MFA on backup console
gives: Repository types, immutability properties, hardened repos, scale-out repos, backup server domain-joined, console roles/MFA; Azure vault soft delete and immutability.
manual: Offsite copy path verification; separate credentials for backup infrastructure.
why: Modern ransomware deletes backups first; E8 ML1 requires backups protected from modification/deletion.
target: Immutable offsite copy; backup infrastructure isolated from production AD.

control: Restore testing: file, VM and application-level restores tested in the last 6 months with evidence; DR runbook exercised annually
gives: SureBackup jobs and last results.
manual: Restore test evidence (tickets / LOG.md) per tier; DR test report.
why: E8 RB ML1: restoration tested as part of DR exercises. Untested backups are hope, not a control.
target: Evidence of restore tests <= 6 months; DR test <= 12 months.

control: Application-consistent backups: SQL/Exchange/AD with VSS and log truncation; AD system state and forest-recovery capability; DC snapshot policy
gives: Jobs without application-aware processing, last AD system-state backup per partition (repadmin /showbackup), long-lived snapshots. ExchangeOnPrem: Mailbox database LastFullBackup age and circular logging state - evidence that an Exchange-aware backup is actually running and truncating logs.
manual: DC snapshot-revert prohibition documented.
why: Crash-consistent images of databases and DCs restore into corruption.
target: App-aware on all DB/AD workloads; AD recoverable.

control: Endpoint and user data protection: OneDrive Known Folder Move enforced, no critical data on local drives or personal cloud, laptop loss scenario covered
gives: Intune ADMX Known Folder Move settings, third-party sync clients on hosts.
manual: OneDrive usage report; Defender for Cloud Apps discovery for unsanctioned storage.
why: Desktop and Documents folders are where the finance spreadsheets actually live.
target: KFM enforced; unsanctioned storage addressed.

control: DR plan and BCP: documented plan with system priorities, RTO tiers, failover procedure (emPOWER DRaaS / ASR / rebuild), dependency map (DNS, identity, licensing), contact tree, reviewed <= 12 months
manual: DR/BCP document (SNOW KB / SharePoint) date and content; emPOWER DRaaS / ASR configuration (Azure ASR items appear in AZ-05); contact tree.
why: Backups without a plan produce a 5-day outage instead of a 5-hour one.
target: Current plan, configured failover for tier-1, annual review.

control: Backup platform lifecycle: Veeam version in support, repository capacity >= 6 months growth headroom, backup server OS supported, licences current
gives: Veeam build and licence/support expiry, repository capacity, backup server OS support.
why: The backup server is often the oldest, least-patched box in the room.
target: Supported, licensed, >= 6 months capacity.

control: Configuration backups of platforms: firewall/switch configs, Entra/Intune/CA policy exports, Azure resource templates, hypervisor config - versioned and restorable
manual: FortiManager revision history / Orion NCM for network configs; Intune/Entra exports (M365DSC or scripted) and Azure templates in a versioned store.
why: Rebuilding a tenant's Conditional Access from memory during an incident is not a plan.
target: All platforms exported <= 30 days, stored securely.

control: BAMS inclusions reconciled: PowerBI 'eFO People or Items in My Org - with ROLES' vs actual devices/services - every billed item exists, every managed item is billed, BAMS codes correct
gives: Inventories to diff against the billing extract: AD servers, Intune devices, host results (hosts.csv), Azure VMs.
manual: PowerBI 'eFO People or Items in My Org - with ROLES'; eFO Cloud Services; SNOW CIs; raise differences with SDM/CAM.
why: Handbook priority 13 (quarterly). Revenue leakage and billing for decommissioned items both damage the relationship.
target: Zero unexplained differences; corrections raised.

control: Monitoring coverage: every server, network device and critical service in Orion (LogicMonitor for cloud); muted/unmanaged nodes justified (they still consume licences)
gives: Hosts unreachable over WinRM (management gaps), Azure alert rules/action groups.
manual: Orion node list vs inventory; unmanaged/muted nodes with reasons; Catalogue Tasks for onboarding.
why: Unmonitored = discovered by the client. Handbook: validate monitoring before handover.
target: 100% of in-scope CIs monitored; muted list clean.

control: Monitoring quality: application/service monitors for critical apps (not just ping/CPU), thresholds tuned, top alerters reviewed, alerts map to runbooks, SSL/domain/backup monitors present
manual: Orion application monitors for tier-1 apps, 30-day alert history/top alerters, NOC runbooks (SNOW KB), certificate/backup monitors.
why: Noisy or shallow monitoring trains the NOC to ignore the real one.
target: Service-level monitoring for all tier-1 apps; noise actioned.

control: Patching coverage: every server and endpoint in an N-Central patch policy; devices not checked in > 30 days; approvals and windows documented; exclusions justified
gives: RMM/management agent presence per host and hosts without one.
manual: N-Central: device list, patch policy membership, last check-in, exclusions with reasons.
why: Patching only works on the devices the tool can see.
target: 100% policy membership; < 3% stale agents; exclusions dated.

control: Security tooling coverage vs contract: EDR, Huntress, Rapid7, Airlock, Mimecast seat counts vs devices/users; agents missing; SIEM log sources (DCs, firewalls, M365) actually ingesting
gives: EDR/MDR/RMM/app-control agent coverage per host with missing lists; Intune remote tools; Defender alert backlog.
manual: Licensed seat counts (eFO subscriptions) vs deployed; Rapid7 IDR data-collection health; Huntress portal; Airlock/Mimecast seat counts.
why: Paid-for seats not deployed are both a security gap and an awkward renewal conversation.
target: Deployed = licensed = devices; all core log sources live.

control: Ticket and incident trends: last 90 days incidents by CI/category, repeat offenders raised as problem records, P1/P2 count, SLA breaches, noisy CIs recorded in PROBLEMS.md
manual: SNOW incident report (last 90 days by CI/category), SLA breaches, problem records; PROBLEMS.md signatures.
why: Recurring incidents are the cheapest improvement opportunities and the client's lived experience of bA.
target: Top repeat issues have problem records and owners.

control: Change and configuration discipline: changes go through RFCs, CIs updated after changes, config drift reports (Orion NCM / FortiManager) reviewed, unauthorised change evidence investigated
manual: SNOW change records vs FortiManager/NCM revision history; CI updates after builds/decoms.
why: Undocumented change is the most common root cause in post-incident reviews.
target: Changes traceable to RFCs; drift reviewed monthly.

control: bA access hygiene: bA credentials in CyberArk customer safe current and rotating, RDM nodes valid, no stale bA accounts in client AD/Entra, GDAP not expiring, offboarded engineers removed
gives: bA-named accounts visible in privileged role/group lists (Entra roles, AD privileged users).
manual: CyberArk rotation dates (customer safe), RDM node validity, GDAP expiry (Lighthouse), squad roster comparison.
why: bA's own access is part of the client's attack surface and is in scope for their auditors.
target: Only current staff, rotated credentials, GDAP > 90 days.

control: Escalation and contact matrix current: client technical/business/after-hours contacts, vendor support contracts and numbers (ISP, Fortinet, Microsoft, LoB vendors), CrowdStrike uninstall-key process, documented in SNOW account and PROFILE.md
manual: SNOW customer account contacts, PROFILE.md, vendor contracts/support numbers, CrowdStrike uninstall-key process.
why: P1s are lost in the first 30 minutes looking for a phone number.
target: Verified in last 6 months.

control: Reporting and cadence delivered: monthly Intune/M365 usage and Defender reports issued and read, quarterly M365 Health Report top-3 acted on, operational/strategic meetings held on cadence
manual: Report folder (SharePoint), LOG.md meeting entries, COMMITMENTS.md, PROFILE.md meeting cadence.
why: Reports that are generated but not discussed are cost without value; the cadence is where billable work is agreed.
target: Cadence held; actions tracked to closure.

control: Essential Eight target maturity agreed with the client (ML1 baseline; ML2 for regulated/critical) and documented; exceptions register with compensating controls
gives: Secure Score category gaps as a conversation starter.
manual: Client's agreed E8 target and exceptions register (PROFILE.md strategic notes / board paper).
why: A target turns the E8 from a scorecard into a plan and makes remediation fundable.
target: Target agreed in writing; exceptions documented.

control: MDR/SOC and detection: Huntress (endpoint + M365 ITDR) and/or Rapid7 IDR deployed with full coverage, response hours defined, alert-to-action process, log retention >= 12 months
gives: MDR agent coverage per host (Huntress/Rapid7), Defender alert backlog and age.
manual: Huntress / Rapid7 IDR console: coverage, log sources, response hours, alert-to-action times, retention.
why: E8 ML2 expects events analysed in a timely manner; detection without response capacity is theatre.
target: Coverage 100%, defined response, core sources logging.

control: Central logging and log protection: event logs centralised (Rapid7/Sentinel/other), protected from tampering, MFA/privileged/application-control events logged, PowerShell and command-line logging (E8 ML2)
gives: PowerShell/command-line logging and Security log size/clearing on hosts; Azure Activity Log diagnostic settings.
manual: SIEM log sources and retention (Rapid7 IDR / Sentinel); Entra sign-in/audit log export (diagnostic settings).
why: Without protected central logs, incident scope cannot be determined and insurers will not pay.
target: Central, protected, >= 12 months, ML2 event classes captured.

control: Vulnerability management programme: authenticated scanning across servers, endpoints and network devices (Rapid7 IVM / Defender VM), cadence per E8 ML1, remediation SLAs tracked, exception process
gives: Azure Update Manager assessment, host patch age, known-vulnerable software versions.
manual: Rapid7 InsightVM / Defender Vulnerability Management: scope vs inventory, scan cadence, ageing, exceptions, remediation SLAs.
why: E8 ML1 mandates scanning cadence; unowned findings age silently.
target: Full-scope scanning on cadence; SLAs met; exceptions dated.

control: External attack surface and credential exposure: LionGard/Rapid7 external view, leaked-credential monitoring for the domain, look-alike domain watch
manual: LionGard / Rapid7 external scan for unknown assets; HIBP domain search; DMARC reports for look-alike domains (domain list is in raw/dns.domains.json).
why: Attackers start from the outside; so should the review.
target: No unknown external assets; breached credentials remediated.

control: Security awareness: phishing simulation and training programme running (Huntress SAT / KnowBe4 / Defender Attack Simulation), report-phish button deployed, results trending
manual: Training platform reports (Huntress SAT / KnowBe4 / Defender Attack Simulation); report-message add-in deployment.
why: Users are the control of last resort for BEC and consent phishing.
target: Quarterly campaigns; click rate trending down; reporting in use.

control: Incident response readiness: client IR plan and bA runbook exist, roles and contacts, cyber-insurance conditions met (MFA, EDR, backups, patching), OAIC notifiable-data-breach and ASD reporting obligations understood, tabletop exercised
manual: IR plan and bA runbook (SNOW KB), insurer conditions (client), tabletop record (LOG.md).
why: E8 ML2 requires an IR plan to be enacted; insurers now audit the conditions they underwrote.
target: Plan < 12 months, insurer conditions evidenced, tabletop annually.

control: Privileged access process (E8 RAP): requests validated on first grant, revalidated at 12 months, disabled after 45 days inactivity (ML2), privileged accounts have no internet/email, break-glass/service/local admin credentials long, unique and managed
gives: Privileged accounts with mailbox/licence, privileged AD accounts inactive > 45 days, password-never-expires, role breakdown.
manual: Access request records (SNOW) and 12-month revalidation evidence.
why: RAP is the E8 strategy most dependent on process rather than product; process is what auditors test.
target: Process evidenced; no stale privileged accounts; admins isolated from email/web.

control: Governance and compliance drivers: information security / acceptable use / access policies current; obligations identified (Privacy Act reforms, APRA CPS 234, SOCI, ISO 27001, PCI DSS); cyber-insurance renewal date known
manual: Client policy set and review dates; obligations (Privacy Act, APRA CPS 234, SOCI, ISO 27001, PCI); insurance renewal month.
why: Drivers determine the target maturity and who pays for remediation.
target: Drivers documented; policies < 24 months old.

control: Physical and environmental: comms/server room access control, UPS runtime and battery age, cooling and environmental monitoring, cabling labelled, camera coverage
manual: Site visit / Field Services report; UPS management card in Orion (battery age, runtime).
why: A failed UPS battery is the most common cause of an unplanned full outage in mid-market.
target: Monitored UPS with batteries < 4 years; controlled access; environmental alerts.

control: Defender / Secure Score remediation tracked: monthly Defender report recommendations (ASR first, then client-prioritised) have owners; risk-accepted items marked in the portal
gives: Secure Score improvement actions with unrealised points, ranked.
manual: Disposition of the last monthly Defender report; risk-accepted items marked in the portal.
why: Handbook: Defender recommendations are outside BAMS remediation scope - they are the billable pipeline if tracked, noise if not.
target: Every recommendation has a disposition and owner.

control: Third-party and vendor remote access: inventory of vendors with access (VPN accounts, TeamViewer/AnyDesk/ScreenConnect, RMM), MFA and time-bounding, monitoring, unsanctioned remote tools blocked
gives: Remote-access tools installed/running per host, Intune-detected remote tools, VPN local users. Nps: the RADIUS client list - every device permitted to ask NPS to authenticate a user - and whether NPS accounting is on, which is the only record of who got onto the network from where.
manual: Vendor access register; firewall logs for vendor sessions.
why: Vendor remote tools are the supply-chain door left open; application control should close the unsanctioned ones.
target: Every vendor path documented, MFA'd and reviewed; unsanctioned tools blocked.

control: Azure governance: subscriptions and management groups documented, tagging (owner, cost centre, environment) enforced, naming standard, resource locks on critical resources, Azure Lighthouse delegation to bA
gives: Subscriptions, resource counts, tag coverage, locks, management groups, Lighthouse registrations.
why: Ungoverned subscriptions grow cost and risk quietly; Lighthouse (KB0016370) is how bA supports them properly.
target: Documented, tagged >= 90%, locked, delegated.

control: Azure RBAC and identities: Owner/Contributor at subscription scope limited and named, PIM for Azure roles where licensed, no classic administrators, service principal secrets/certificates with expiry tracked, managed identities preferred
gives: Owner/Contributor/UAA at subscription scope, direct user assignments, classic admins, service principals; app registration credentials expiring/long-lived.
manual: PIM for Azure roles configuration (P2).
why: Subscription Owner is the cloud equivalent of Domain Admin.
target: Least privilege, group-based, PIM'd; secrets tracked.

control: Azure cost management: budgets and alerts set, monthly spend trend, Advisor cost recommendations actioned (right-size, reservations/savings plans, orphaned disks/IPs/NICs, stopped-not-deallocated VMs), Hybrid Benefit applied
gives: 6-month spend by month, budgets per subscription, Advisor cost savings, orphaned disks/NICs/IPs, stopped-not-deallocated VMs, Hybrid Benefit usage.
why: Cloud cost optimisation is the most welcome value-add conversation a PE can start.
target: Budget alerts on; Advisor cost items dispositioned; no orphaned spend.

control: Azure security posture: Defender for Cloud secure score, Defender plans on for servers/SQL/storage where warranted, JIT VM access, no public RDP/SSH in NSGs, storage accounts not anonymous, TLS 1.2 minimum, secrets in Key Vault, diagnostics to Log Analytics
gives: Defender for Cloud score and high-severity recommendations, NSG internet exposure, storage public access/TLS/network, Key Vault purge protection, Defender plans, Activity Log diagnostics.
why: Exposed management ports and public storage are the two most exploited Azure misconfigurations.
target: No internet-exposed management ports; storage locked; diagnostics on; plans enabled for tier-1.

control: Azure resilience and backup: Azure Backup on all VMs with soft delete/immutability, ASR or availability zones for tier-1, PaaS SQL PITR/geo-redundancy aligned to RPO, VM agents and extensions healthy
gives: VMs without backup items, failed/old backups, vault soft delete/immutability/redundancy, ASR replication health.
manual: PaaS SQL PITR/geo-redundancy per database if in scope.
why: Cloud does not mean backed up; E8 RB applies equally to IaaS.
target: 100% VM coverage; immutable; tier-1 DR configured.

control: Azure networking: topology documented (hub/spoke or single VNet), NSG/ASG hygiene, Azure Firewall/NVA where needed, VPN/ExpressRoute redundancy, private endpoints for PaaS, private DNS design, public IP inventory
gives: Public IP inventory, storage/Key Vault network defaults.
manual: Network Watcher topology, VPN/ExpressRoute redundancy, private endpoints per PaaS service, private DNS design.
why: Cloud networks accumulate the same flat-network problems as on-prem, faster.
target: Documented, segmented, private endpoints for data services, redundant connectivity.

control: Azure operations: Azure Monitor alerts (VM heartbeat, disk, backup failure, cost) routed to bA (LogicMonitor), Azure Update Manager schedules, Arc for on-prem servers if in scope, Azure Policy baseline (allowed locations, required tags)
gives: Policy compliance and assignments, alert rules and action groups, Update Manager assessments, Arc machines, monitor agents.
manual: Confirm action-group destinations reach bA (LogicMonitor).
why: Azure resources without alert routing are unmonitored in every way that matters (COV-02 for cloud).
target: Alerts to bA, patching scheduled, policy baseline assigned.

control: Other cloud and SaaS: AWS/GCP footprint (if any) with equivalent controls; critical SaaS inventory (owner, SSO, backup, contract, data location); shadow IT discovery via Defender for Cloud Apps or firewall logs
gives: Sync clients and shadow-IT hints from device inventories; Enterprise applications count.
manual: Defender for Cloud Apps discovery; SaaS register built with the client; AWS/GCP inventory.
why: The ERP in someone's credit-card SaaS is a business risk nobody owns.
target: Register exists; tier-1 SaaS on SSO with backup; shadow IT reviewed.

control: Critical infrastructure documentation currency: per-customer SNOW KB articles for AD, network, backup, firewall and key apps updated within 1 month of change; services docs within 3 months; as-builts for recent projects
manual: SNOW Knowledge per-customer KBs (last modified vs last change), SharePoint Technical folder, Confluence legacy content.
why: Handbook priority 14; stale docs are the first thing a P1 exposes.
target: All critical docs within currency windows; nothing critical left in Confluence only.

control: Architecture and network diagrams current, versioned in SharePoint Technical docs, and linked from SNOW KB
manual: SharePoint Technical docs diagrams (version/date) and SNOW KB links.
why: Handbook: network changes must update diagrams and fix links to versioned docs.
target: Current, versioned, linked.

control: Credential handling: all client credentials in CyberArk customer safes, none in documents, tickets, email or Confluence; rotation on staff exit (both sides); break-glass procedure documented
manual: CyberArk PVWA customer safe; keyword sweep of SNOW KB / SharePoint / Confluence for credentials; rotation after staff changes.
why: Credentials in KBs and tickets are the finding that ends a contract.
target: Zero credentials outside the vault; rotation evidenced.

control: Runbooks and known-issue KBs: top 5 recurring ticket types have KBs, P1 runbooks exist (DR failover, ISP failover, EDR uninstall key, tenant lock-out), problem records for recurring issues
manual: SNOW KB coverage of the top recurring ticket types, P1 runbooks, problem records.
why: Handbook escalation rule: would better documentation have prevented this? Usually yes.
target: KBs for top-5; P1 runbooks complete; problem records raised.

control: Configuration management: SNOW CIs accurate (owner, environment, criticality, IP/NAT IP), relationships/dependency map for tier-1 services, eFO/SNOW sync gaps closed
gives: Inventories with OS/IP/role that serve as the truth side for CI accuracy.
manual: SNOW CMDB sample of 10 CIs; eFO/SNOW sync gaps; tier-1 dependency map.
why: CI quality drives impact assessment in change and incident; the sync gap is a known handbook issue.
target: Complete CIs; tier-1 dependency map; no sync gaps.

control: Standards documented: SOE/build standards, naming conventions, patch and change windows, maintenance calendar, client-specific decommission guide
gives: GPO inventory and unlinked GPOs, Intune update rings (patch windows).
manual: SOE/build standards, naming conventions, maintenance calendar, decommission guide (SNOW KB / SharePoint).
why: Standards make work repeatable by any engineer, not just the one who knows.
target: All six exist and match practice.

control: Knowledge risk: single points of knowledge (client side and bA side), documented split of responsibilities (client IT vs bA RACI), informal 'helpers' with admin rights identified
manual: PROFILE.md contacts/roles, RACI in SoW; informal admins (use IAM-05 and local-admin evidence as prompts).
why: The most fragile part of most environments is one person.
target: SPOKs named and mitigated; RACI documented.

control: Licence and contract records: software licence register (Microsoft CSP/EA, VMware, Veeam, Fortinet, Adobe, LoB apps) with proof and renewal dates; SoW/BAMS scope accessible to the squad
manual: Licence register (SharePoint Commercial), eFO annuity, vendor portals; collectors supply Entra SKUs and Veeam/vSphere/FortiGate licence data as inputs.
why: Renewal surprises and true-up exposure are avoidable with a register.
target: Register complete; every renewal owned.

control: Risk communication: technical risks with business consequence recorded (OPPORTUNITIES.md / client risk register), formally notified to SDM and CAM with dates, client risk-acceptance recorded where declined
manual: OPPORTUNITIES.md, COMMITMENTS.md, notification emails/Teams messages to SDM and CAM.
why: Handbook priority 5: risks -> SDM & CAM. A risk not written down is bA's risk.
target: All High risks notified and dispositioned.

control: Hardware lifecycle register: servers, storage, network, UPS, endpoints - purchase date, warranty/support end, replacement year, budget signalled to SDM/CAM
gives: Manufacturer/model/serial per host and hypervisor host hardware (inputs to the register).
manual: Warranty lookups (Dell/HP) by serial, Fortinet/Meraki/Aruba EoS, purchase dates, FY budget mapping.
why: Refresh projects are the most predictable billable pipeline and the most avoidable outages.
target: Register current; nothing out of support without a plan.

control: Software and OS lifecycle register: Windows/Server/SQL/Exchange/vSphere/Veeam/FortiOS versions with EoS dates; anything already past EoS (e.g. SQL 2016 since 14 Jul 2026, vSphere 7 since 2 Oct 2025) or within 12 months (e.g. Server 2016 on 12 Jan 2027) flagged
gives: OS/SQL/Exchange/vSphere/Veeam/FortiOS versions with support status and EoS dates where known. ExchangeOnPrem: Exchange version and end-of-support date per server for the lifecycle register.
manual: Consolidate into the register; vendor lifecycle pages for network gear and LoB apps.
why: E8 PO/PA require unsupported software removed; planning 12 months out turns emergencies into projects.
target: Register current; every < 12-month item has a plan.

control: Renewals calendar: M365 CSP/NCE anniversaries, FortiCare/FortiGuard, Meraki/Aruba Central, Veeam, EDR/Huntress/Rapid7/Mimecast, domains and certificates - items > 90 days out surfaced to SDM/CAM
gives: FortiGuard/FortiCare, vSphere and Veeam licence expiry; M365 SKU list. Citrix: licence inventory with counts in use, expiry and Subscription Advantage / Customer Success Services date. ParallelsRas: licence type, status, expiry and concurrent-user headroom.
manual: eFO annuity (NCE anniversaries), Meraki/Aruba Central, EDR/Huntress/Rapid7/Mimecast terms, GeoCerts, TPP. NetScaler subscription (Advanced/Premium) expiry is not read over NITRO - take it from the appliance's licence page. Citrix on-premises file-based licensing reached end of life on 15 Apr 2026 - confirm the client has moved to the License Activation Service.
why: Lapsed FortiGuard or Central licences silently disable security features; NCE terms lock pricing.
target: Calendar complete; nothing lapses unplanned.

control: Licence compliance and optimisation: M365 assigned vs active, Windows Server/RDS CALs, SQL core licensing on VMs, VMware subscription status, Azure Hybrid Benefit; true-up exposure
gives: Unassigned M365 seats, licensed inactive/shared mailboxes, Hybrid Benefit, Advisor savings.
manual: RDS CALs, SQL core licensing vs VMs, VMware subscription terms.
why: Both over-spend and non-compliance are findings the client will thank you for.
target: No material non-compliance; savings identified and proposed.

control: Technology roadmap: 12-24 month roadmap agreed with the client (refreshes, migrations, security uplift), aligned to business drivers, reviewed quarterly with SDM/CAM, feeding eFO opportunities
manual: Roadmap document / last technology report, OPPORTUNITIES.md, eFO leads.
why: Handbook priority 15: find billable items -> leads. A roadmap is the structured version of that.
target: Roadmap exists, current, and every item has a lead or decision.

control: Capacity and budget cycle: headcount/site change plans, storage and bandwidth growth, M365 storage quotas, client financial year and budget submission dates captured so proposals land before budgeting
manual: PROFILE.md (FY, budget month), SDM briefing, growth signals; M365 storage reports.
why: A good proposal delivered after the budget closes waits a year.
target: Budget window known; proposals timed.

control: Contract scope fit: BAMS inclusions vs what the client actually needs; out-of-scope work being absorbed as BAU (leakage); unused inclusions; SLA and after-hours coverage fit
manual: SoW/BAMS schedule vs LOG.md billable fields and SNOW time entries; unused inclusions; SLA misfit examples.
why: Scope drift is unbilled effort on one side and churn risk on the other.
target: Scope matches reality; leakage quantified and raised.

control: Strategic risks logged: top risks with business consequence in OPPORTUNITIES.md and client risk register, communicated to SDM and CAM with dates, acceptance recorded when declined
manual: OPPORTUNITIES.md / client risk register, COMMITMENTS.md, notification dates.
why: Closes the loop on the review: every High finding becomes a decision someone owns.
target: All P1/P2 findings dispositioned.
